description: The DEFAULT constraint with CURRENT_TIMESTAMP / CURRENT_DATE (with and without parentheses), through the SQL surface - the DESCRIBE TABLE default cell plus the populated values themselves, read back with server-side predicates (IS NOT NULL, = CURRENT_DATE) so the clock and time zone are the executing engine's own: auto-population on INSERT (single, multiple, reordered column list, multi-row VALUES), an explicit NULL overriding the default, literal defaults alongside, multiple defaulted columns, and both syntax forms mixed in one table. Converted 1:1 from features/DefaultCurrentTimestampTest (now retired).

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE test_timestamps (id INTEGER, created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, name VARCHAR)
DESCRIBE TABLE test_timestamps
SELECT CONTAINS(UPPER(MAX(IFF("name" = 'CREATED_AT', "default", NULL))), 'CURRENT_TIMESTAMP') FROM TABLE(RESULT_SCAN(LAST_QUERY_ID()))
CREATE TABLE test_timestamps (id INTEGER, created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, name VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO test_timestamps (id, name) VALUES (1, 'Alice')
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM test_timestamps WHERE id = 1 AND created_at IS NOT NULL
